svg.text: What a JDWP attach can see on Android, and what it cannot
Everything runs in one ART process, so the attach sees every class the app loaded. That is nearly all of it, and the
one exception is absolute rather than awkward.
Your common-module Java
breakpoints work out of the box
The CN1 Attach Android run config is scoped to this module, so the IDE resolves both the source
pane and the variables view from its classpath.
Your android-module Java or Kotlin
native interfaces, Activities, helpers
Breakpoints work here too. Remote JVM Debug does not restrict which module they live in.
See the note below if the variables view looks empty.
Codename One framework code
core and the Android port
AndroidImplementation, CodenameOneActivity and the rest are ordinary loaded classes. They need
source resolution pointed at the Codename One sources before the IDE will show them.
Native C or C++ through the NDK
not on this path at all
JDWP only speaks JVM, so no attach here reaches it. Attach Android Studio's LLDB to the same
process instead -- the two are independent and run side by side against one device.
An empty variables view is a classpath, not a failed breakpoint
The run config's module setting does not decide where breakpoints may live. It decides whose classpath the IDE uses to
display state, so stopping in android-module code with the common module selected shows a stop with nothing in it.
